Baltic Exchange Market Report 07 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3034 (43)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5139 (65)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2195 (60)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1521 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 827 (3)
CAPESIZE
A slightly mixed day for the market as participants appeared to reassess current levels. The BCI 182 5TC gained a further $593 to close at $46,610. C5 remained relatively flat with only a marginal gain of $0.005 to $15.715, while C3 drifted sideways with a slight decline of $0.104 to $36.805. In the Pacific, the market developed a more positional tone throughout the session. Offers on C5 started the day in the low to mid-$16s, with premiums continuing to be paid for earlier laycans around 19–21 May, where reports suggested low $16s were achieved. However, for later dates around 25/26 May, rates closer to $15.50 were repeated more than once, highlighting the widening spread between prompt and forward positions. Despite the softer undertone later in the day, the presence of all three miners on C5 continued to provide a degree of support. The Atlantic was described by many as “standoff-ish,” with limited urgency from either side and minimal bids seen on C3. Even so, tonnage lists in both basins remain tight, preventing any meaningful downside pressure for now. Bunker prices softened as Brent crude moved lower amid growing optimism surrounding a potential easing of Middle East tensions and renewed US-Iran negotiations.
PANAMAX
Today has seen another positive session across both basins in the Panamax market with the P5TC increasing by $542 to $19,758. The Atlantic is reported to be maintaining firm sentiment with brokers highlighting a tightening tonnage list alongside a steady increase in cargo supply while prompt positions are becoming notably scarce. Fixture activity has picked up, with rates showing improvement on previously concluded levels. Industry sources have also pointed to continued support in the fronthaul market, with a consistent flow of grain cargoes underpinning bid levels and driving fixtures upward. In the Pacific, brokers note that the North Pacific and Australian markets remain tight on available tonnage, with charterers struggling to secure firm offers from owners. Mineral trades continue to lead the upside in rates, although some grain fixtures have also been reported. Indonesia remains active with underlying fundamentals still imbalanced as brokers highlight a shortage of larger, modern vessels willing to commit to shorter duration voyages. Messrs Avenir were linked with the scrubber fitted Oceana (81,528 2014) open in Fangcheng 11/12 May for a trip to India with limestone at $22,500, while the Efraim A (82,174 2010) open Machong 11 May was reported as fixed to Aequor for a trip from Indonesia to India.
SUPRAMAX
A rather muted day across the board. IN the Atlantic there seemed to be a difference of opinion as to the opportunities for the owners’ side in the US Gulf, some saying fundamentals remain healthy whilst others are a bit more sceptical. Like the larger sisters in the South Atlantic remained relatively positive although little fresh fixing surfaced. From Asia, brokers spoke of a good volume of fresh cargo entering into the market which helped keep positive momentum although some felt maybe a ceiling was being seen from the north. An ultramax was heard to have been fixed basis delivery Busan for a NoPac round redelivery Chittagong at below $17,000 but no more details came to light. Elsewhere, the Ae Venus (56,847 2009) was heard to have been fixed basis delivery Durban trip Vietnam at $17,000 plus $700,000 ballast bonus. Further north, the Gul Bano (58,091 2010) was heard fixed at around $20,000 levels basis delivery Mongla for EC India to WC India coastal with coal. Similarly, the PVT Topaz (57,318 2009)was also heard fixed at around $20,000 levels delivery Visakhapatnam also for a coastal EC India to WC India, again further details remained lacking. The 11TC average closed today up $90, at $19,226.
HANDYSIZE
The market saw mixed performance today, with sentiment largely shaped by positional factors. The BHSI gained 3 points, reaching 827, while the 7TC average settled at $14,888. The trend from yesterday persisted across the Continent and Mediterranean, where new inquiries were limited, resulting in subdued activity. Over in the US Gulf and South Atlantic, there has been a bit more movement, with some activity and fresh demand coming through. However, it hasn't been enough to absorb the excess tonnage available, so rates are holding steady for the time being and overall sentiment remains firm. Notable fixtures include the CS Jenna (37,713 2015), which was fixed from Santos to Morocco with sugars by Alvean Sugar on voyage terms, although further details weren’t disclosed. Similarly, the Clipper Mallorca (40,313 2025) was fixed from South Brazil to the UK-Portugal range with sugar in the $22,000’s, with differential for UK and Lisbon redelivery by Berge Bulk, but specifics remain limited. Similarly, the Asian market remained flat today. Some reports indicate a slightly longer tonnage list, but the cargo book has shown little change, and rates are staying close to the last done levels with no significant deviations.

Market Fundamentals
Australia Launches Strategic Fuel Reserves

Australia is establishing a 1 billion litre Fuel Security Reserve to boost long-term supplies of diesel and aviation fuel for the mining industry and broader economy, McCloskey reports. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the package "will provide more than AUD 10bn to secure Australia's near term fuel and fertiliser security, and lift the Minimum Stockholding Obligation by around 10 days for every type of fuel." The goal is to increase on-shore fuel reserves to at least 50 days' supply for diesel and aviation fuel, though the International Energy Agency recommends 90 days of net oil imports. The extra 10 days of holdings will cost AUD 34.7 million over four years.
Australia's mining industry consumes 9.6 billion litres of diesel annually, according to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). Mining companies receive a diesel tax rebate estimated at AUD 1.5 billion per year to coal miners, the IEEFA reported.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Pressure on the Cape FFA curve continued to mount today, despite the index gaining another $593. The May and Jun contracts lost the most value with 38500 and 34750 sold respectively, in response to reports of 35.50 being fixed C3 during the afternoon session. Despite this, the May v Jun widened and strengthened up to a high of 4000. Q3 lacked liquidity today with a range of 31400-31700 and similarly the Q4 with 31000 sold. The Cal27 was fairly active with 26050 trading early on, then hit back down to 25900. Activity on the Cal28 was sporadic with 22850 trading several times and then eventually sold down to 22800 as the rest of the curve continued to weaken.

PMX
PMX traded flat today, with minor improvements across the front of the curve. May traded at a low of 20250 and was bid up to 20700 and dropped to 20600 by the close. June moved from 20600 to 21000, while the May+June strip traded between 20500 and 20750. July printed from 20100 to 20500, while August improved to 20150 falling back to 19950. Q3 traded in a narrow range of 19800 to 20000, and Q4 traded around 18000. On the back end, Cal27 traded at 14,950 and 15,000 today.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX market held steady today, with most of the focus on June and the Cal. May traded within a tight $200 range, moving between 17850 and 18050. June strengthened to 18700 before finishing the day at 18500, while July traded between 18150 and 18300. August saw a few clips clear at 18000, while Q3 traded from 17700 to 17800, and Q4 was bid up to 16100. Cal27 saw good participation today, trading between 13250 and 13350.

Carbon
EU carbon markets declined 1.3% in fairly quiet trading. During the assessment window, the benchmark Dec26 EUA futures contract was trading at �75.14/eua, down �0.97.

Today's auction provided some morning support to the futures market, settling 2.7m EUAs at �74.72/eua, which was a premium to last night's daily spot futures close and over �2 above Tuesday's auction. However, while the futures market opened higher, with little news emerging from the Arabian Gulf or regional energy markets, carbon prices moved slowly lower in the afternoon to close down on the day.

Market Fundamentals
Australia Launches Strategic Fuel Reserves
Australia is establishing a 1 billion litre Fuel Security Reserve
to boost long-term supplies of diesel and aviation fuel for the
mining industry and broader economy, McCloskey reports.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the package "will
provide more than AUD 10bn to secure Australia's near term
fuel and fertiliser security, and lift the Minimum Stockholding
Obligation by around 10 days for every type of fuel." The
goal is to increase on-shore fuel reserves to at least 50 days'
supply for diesel and aviation fuel, though the International
Energy Agency recommends 90 days of net oil imports. The
extra 10 days of holdings will cost AUD 34.7 million over four
years.
Australia's mining industry consumes 9.6 billion litres of
diesel annually, according to the Institute for Energy
Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). Mining companies
receive a diesel tax rebate estimated at AUD 1.5 billion per
year to coal miners, the IEEFA reported.

The C5 market opened with strong activity across the curve
this morning. June traded at 14.00, July at 13.25, and August
at 13.00. Further out, October, November, and December
traded outright at 12.60, 12.65, and 12.70 respectively, while
Q4 softened to 12.50. On the longer-dated contracts, January
traded at 10.40 and March at 10.90. In the C3 market, there
was notable sell-side interest in the front months, although
no trades were reported.
Cape
Pressure on the Cape FFA curve continued to mount today,
despite the index gaining another $593. The May and Jun
contracts lost the most value with 38500 and 34750 sold
respectively, in response to reports of 35.50 being ﬁxed C3
during the afternoon session. Despite this, the May v Jun
widened and strengthened up to a high of 4000. Q3 lacked
liquidity today with a range of 31400-31700 and similarly the
Q4 with 31000 sold. The Cal27 was fairly active with 26050
trading early on, then hit back down to 25900. Activity on the
Cal28 was sporadic with 22850 trading several times and
then eventually sold down to 22800 as the rest of the curve
continued to weaken.
PMX

front of the curve. May traded at a low of 20250 and was bid
up to 20700 and dropped to 20600 by the close. June moved
from 20600 to 21000, while the May+June strip traded
between 20500 and 20750. July printed from 20100 to 20500,
while August improved to 20150 falling back to 19950. Q3
traded in a narrow range of 19800 to 20000, and Q4 traded
around 18000. On the back end, Cal27 traded at 14,950 and
15,000 today.
SMX + HANDY

June and the Cal. May traded within a tight $200 range,
moving between 17850 and 18050. June strengthened to
18700 before ﬁnishing the day at 18500, while July traded
between 18150 and 18300. August saw a few clips clear at
18000, while Q3 traded from 17700 to 17800, and Q4 was bid
up to 16100. Cal27 saw good participation today, trading

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the package "will provide more than AUD 10bn to secure Australia's near term fuel and fertiliser security, and lift the Minimum Stockholding Obligation by around 10 days for every type of fuel." The goal is to increase on-shore fuel reserves to at least 50 days' supply for diesel and aviation fuel, though the International Energy Agency recommends 90 days of net oil imports. The extra 10 days of holdings will cost AUD 34.7 million over four years. Australia's mining industry consumes 9.6 billion litres of diesel annually, according to the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA). Mining companies receive a diesel tax rebate estimated at AUD 1.5 billion per year to coal miners, the IEEFA reported. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场涨跌互现，Capesize指数受太平洋支撑上涨65点至5139，但FFA曲线远月承压下行；Panamax表现强劲，BPI跳升60点至2195，现货达19758美元，大西洋与太平洋两端均现船舶紧张；Supramax与Handysize趋于平稳。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: BDI收3034升43点，四大船型全线上涨。Capesize太平洋C5航线持稳于15.715美元，西澳至青岛航线有支撑；大西洋C3微跌至36.805美元，市场观望情绪浓。Panamax 5TC升至19758美元，吨位收紧推动费率上行。Supramax 11TC报19226美元，亚洲货盘活跃但北向动能趋缓。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize FFA曲线全线走弱，Jun26合约跌1075美元至34500，Cal27报25800；Panamax FFA前月保持坚挺，May26达20700美元。铁矿即期C5报15.715持稳，C3澳矿至青岛36.805微跌0.104美元。Pacific市场positioning特征明显，prompt与25/26日船舶价差扩大至0.5美元/吨。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注Panamax大西洋短期紧张格局，印尼至印度石灰石航次现船成交22000美元上方。Supramax亚洲区域孟加拉回程航线低于17000美元未见成交，沿海印度煤运维持20000美元水平。Handysize南美糖运活跃，巴西至UK-Portugal航线费率达22000美元。

market_watch: Capesize FFA远月曲线持续承压，Cal27/28合约流动性减弱
Panamax Fronthaul谷物货盘支撑费率，大西洋吨位短缺
印尼煤炭市场小灵便型船舶供应紧张，短期期租费率坚挺
原油回落至Brent下方，布伦特走弱带动船燃成本下行
铁矿C3航线偏弱运行，中澳贸易情绪边际转淡

route_focus.view: Tubarao至青岛航线报36.805美元，小幅回落0.104美元，大西洋端需求平淡，美伊谈判预期缓解地缘风险，油价回落令煤焦支撑减弱，短期偏震荡。
太平洋印尼-印度航线紧张，81-82K船型短缺，Efrain A号即期成交21750美元石灰石航次，大西洋谷物持续支撑fronthaul市场，5TC报19758美元仍有上行空间。
南美至北非/欧洲航线活跃，CS Jenna号完成Santos至摩洛哥糖运，Clipper Mallorca巴西至UK-Portugal成交22000美元上方，小型船市场基本面尚可但吨位供应略显充裕。
